theFix.what: merge-notices.md said the wake-routing table is in skill://legion-architect/SKILL.md, which stopped being true when main's #2192 moved it to references/wake-routing.md. The commit rewrites that one sentence in the source and in the generated claude-envoy copy.
theFix.verified: The new sentence names references/wake-routing.md, which exists and carries the table with this branch's four compressed merge-notice rows and its merge-waiting row. I ran the guard rather than reading the link: packages/pi-legion's skills-guard is 11 pass, 0 fail, 23 expect(), and its brokenSkillLinks case validates both the file and the heading of every skill:// anchor. The bundle copy is cmp-identical to the source for all three architect documents, so it is a rebuild and not a hand edit.
theFix.shape: The sentence names what the reference gives rather than where the table currently sits, so the next relocation does not falsify it again - which is the right fix for a class this branch has now been bitten by twice.

theControl.what: The finding generalised: no surviving claim anywhere that the wake-routing table lives in the architect's SKILL.md, with dated history told apart from live claims rather than counted as hits.
theControl.result: skills/, packages/claude-envoy/legion/ and packages/daemon/internal/prompts/ carry no mention of legion-architect/SKILL.md at all, so there is no live claim of any wording to be stale. The only hits in the tree are under docs/, and I read each rather than counting it: docs/plans/ file lists from 2026-09-10, and docs/solutions/ records that cite the skill for something other than the table's location. The two that come closest are both dated narratives of named commits - INFRA-376's learning reporting main's own move (ten mentions, each about what #2192 did at 14571f6f) and the fingerprint learning citing a table row rewritten during an earlier rebase. Neither tells a reader where the table is now.
theControl.discrimination: The rule I applied, stated because the architect asked whether it holds: a hit is live when a reader would act on it to find something today, and dated when it reports what was true at a named commit or issue. The direct test of the discrimination is that the targeted grep - a wake-routing table named as being in SKILL.md - returns nothing at all, while the broad grep returns ten dated records. A sweep that could not tell them apart would have returned ten false hits here, so the all-clear is not an artefact of a narrow pattern.
theControl.noted: INFRA-376's learning records the skill at 33,651 bytes after the move; it is 33,662 here, the difference being this branch's own edits to that file. A dated figure, right for its commit.

(1) The Retro paragraph says this head carries docs/solutions and the handoff removal and nothing else above the approved a54b7826; the fifth merge, this round's fix and two handoffs are above it now, and the sentence should name 05cd4b22 rather than this head. (2) The boundary paragraph's 'all 76 files of this diff' is the non-handoff count: GitHub reports 79 paths, 76 outside .legion/. (3) The same paragraph's 'every role-prompt change here is a deletion or a pagination flag' overlooks the added notice paragraph in prompts/go/architect-common.md. (4) The sceptical reading offered as boundary evidence - that an hour-after-queue notice is the only place the daemon measures elapsed time to tell a human something - is false as written, and the distinction is worth keeping rather than deleting: Lagging.Stalled measures elapsed time too, but against GitHub's own clock, the pull request's updatedAt, where the new timer measures against the daemon's record of when it acted. 'The only place the daemon measures elapsed time against its own record' is both true and the stronger claim.
